copies.headline: Jeanty And Hall Bury The Gold Standard
copies.body:
The running backs decided this one and it wasn't close: Ashton Jeanty's 27.9 and Breece Hall's 19.0 gave Kaleb 46.9 at the position against Adam's 26.4, a 20.5-point gap in a nine-point game. Adam actually won three spots — WR by 6.9, tight end by 10.5 on Colston Loveland, D/ST by eight while Kaleb's Vikings posted a clean zero — and still lost, because Rico Dowdle's 7.4 and Will Reichard's 3.8 are not how the league's highest-scoring team is supposed to function. Michael Mayer's 1.4 on an 8.9 projection should have sunk Kaleb. It didn't.
Both benches were loud. Ladd McConkey put up 20.7 while Keenan Allen limped to 6.8, and Brock Purdy's 22.2 sat behind Bryce Young's 16.0 — Adam's own margin, gift-wrapped and left in the garage.
We had Adam by 21. We also have Kaleb at 103.7 points per game, dead last, with a 45-76 all-play and +2.9 luck wins. Both 7-5 now. Only one of them earned it.

copies.headline: Tetairoa McMillan Saves Logan From Himself
copies.body:
Logan won this at flex, where Tetairoa McMillan's 19.1 covered for a lineup that otherwise leaked points everywhere. Noah took the backfield 30.9 to 20.6, took tight end, took kicker, and still lost by 2.9, because his receivers managed 8.9 combined. Jordyn Tyson put up 2.0 against an 11.8 projection and Garrett Wilson managed 6.9 on 14.1. Logan wasn't clean either — Jaylen Warren 4.9 on 15.6, Isaiah Likely 4.5 on 13.1, Luther Burden III 3.3 on 15.1. Two bad teams, one slightly less bad on the day.
The bench is what will keep Noah up. Antonio Williams scored 21.2 sitting down while Tyson started and did nothing. That's the game, twice over, in one roster slot. Jaylen Waddle's 9.1 would also have been enough.
Noah falls to 3-8 with a 38-83 all-play, dead last in both, and the postseason assassin won't get a postseason to work with. Logan is 5-6 and scoring like a 4 seed at 119.9 per game. We had him by 19; we'll take 2.9 and the win.

copies.headline: John's Backfield Outruns Christian's Wideouts By Inches
copies.body:
The running backs decided this one, or more precisely Christian's refusal to get any. Jonah Coleman went for 34.9 and Emmett Johnson added 24.3 out of the flex, which gave John 46.8 at RB plus the flex against Christian's 16.9 — Chase Brown managed 8.6 on a 15.6 projection and Bhayshul Tuten, now listed Questionable with an undisclosed issue, put up 8.3 on 16.9. That's roughly 15 points of shortfall from two backs, in a game decided by six-tenths.
Christian's receivers nearly bailed him out anyway. CeeDee Lamb 30.2, Jameson Williams 19.3, George Kittle 18.4 — a 49.5 WR day against John's 15.6, with Xavier Hutchinson contributing 3.3 on a 10.7 projection. But Trevor Lawrence missed by nearly seven, the Bills D/ST edge over the Chargers' 1.0 wasn't enough, and Tyler Bass quietly won it with 17.5. Kickers decide games. It's grim.
We picked Christian by 11, which was wrong in the dullest possible way. John's 6-5 now reads closer to the 80-41 all-play he's been earning all year; Christian, 5-6 with an identical profile, keeps losing games he statistically won.

copies.headline: Texans Defense Beats Isaac By Six
copies.body:
The margin was 6.0 and the Houston D/ST was 15.0 of it. Leif won this game without his quarterback and without his tight end — Josh Allen managed 12.2 against a 23.4 projection, Dalton Schultz turned in 2.1 — and still cleared the bar because Mike Evans went for 22.9, Derrick Henry added 19.1, and the bottom of the roster quietly outscored Isaac's by double digits. Jason Sanders beat Matt Gay by 4.6. Those are the kicker and defense slots deciding a football game, which is exactly the kind of win Leif has been building his season on.
Isaac got the QB edge (+8.3) and the TE edge (+9.4) and lost anyway, because Ja'Marr Chase put up 8.1 on a 25.4 projection and Cam Skattebo gave him 5.8 on 14.5 with Justice Hill scoring 17.6 on the bench. That's the loss, twice over. We picked Isaac by 11 and the Chase number torched it.
Isaac drops to 5-6, two straight losses, all-play 55-66 that says he's roughly who his record says. Leif is 8-3 with +2.6 luck wins and a #9 power ranking — Joey Lunchbox is somehow running a contender.

copies.headline: Kelce and Dak Bury Grant's Middle
copies.body:
Mitchell won this at the positions where Grant had no counterpunch. Travis Kelce put up 25.4 against Chig Okonkwo's 10.6, a 14.8-point gap at the thinnest spot on the roster, and Dak Prescott's 35.9 took another 10.9 off Mahomes. Add Jahmyr Gibbs carrying the backfield to a +11.2 edge and the game was decided before you got to the flex, where both lineups were actively embarrassing. Mitchell's 162.9 is a season high and the third straight week over 128.
Grant didn't collapse so much as flatline. Every starter except Mahomes landed between 5 and 16.4, which is a fine way to lose by 41. Tony Pollard was the one real miss — 11.0 on a 20.8 projection, roughly the size of the RB gap by itself. Caleb Douglas at 5.0 in the flex didn't help.
So Grant falls to 5-6 with a -0.9 luck mark and the fifth-best scoring average, which is the kind of season that makes you check the schedule twice. We had Grant by nine. We were off by fifty. Mitchell, 4-7 and winners of three straight, is doing the thing Mitchell always does: arriving exactly when it stops mattering.

copies.headline: Peter's Backfield No-Shows, CJ Cruises By 39
copies.body:
The running backs decided this before lunch. Chuba Hubbard went for 26.0, and even with Jonathan Taylor laying an egg at 6.7 against a 16.6 projection, CJ's backfield cleared Peter's by 26 points. Kyle Monangai's 1.8 and Emari Demercado's 4.9 is not a committee, it's a vacancy. Peter got 23.8 from George Pickens and roughly nothing anywhere else — Cade Otton also chipped in 1.8, which is a cute symmetry and a miserable tight end score.
The quarterback decision was worse. Kirk Cousins put up 7.4 on a 14.7 projection while Fernando Mendoza scored 22.9 on the bench and Aaron Rodgers sat there with 16.0. That's a 66.3, a new season low, and it's Peter's fourth straight loss. CJ left Devaughn Vele's 14.6 behind and it didn't matter one bit.
We picked CJ by 14 and he beat it by 25. He's 6-5, though a 43% all-play says that record is generous. Peter, the 2022 champ, is 5-6 and sinking toward a familiar wardrobe conversation.

intro: John and Christian combined for 268 points and the whole thing came down to six tenths of a point, which is the kind of margin that turns a Monday night kneel-down into a grudge. Mitchell's 162.9 was the week's actual football, burying Grant by 41.5, while Peter's 66.3 was the week's actual crime scene — CJ beat him by 38.9 and barely had to show up to do it. Elsewhere, Logan survived Noah by 2.9 and Leif got past Isaac by six, so half the slate was decided by less than a stat correction.
